findings: All three use Android accessibility nodes. TB already prefetches window descendants and caches host snapshots by event sequence.

Maestro 2.12.1 refreshes its accessibility cache after waitForIdle(500), dumps hierarchy XML into a gRPC string response, then parses/maps the XML on the host. The idle wait is bounded by 500 ms, not necessarily a fixed 500-ms delay.

Speedrun uses a binary visible-node screen dump, host-side YAML matching, and a short 300-ms reuse window when no intervening agent call occurred. Its normal Android settle combines frame/event observations with main-thread probes. It clears the accessibility cache for Compose too.

Speedrun FIND exists, but the inspected ordinary YAML runner uses SCREEN; FIND is used by a developer benchmark in host/main.odin. Normal field taps use a targeted focus query. Do not attribute the normal flow performance to universal on-device selector execution.

TB forces fresh full reads at 40-ms intervals to protect against event-silent motion, for up to two seconds. The profiled login_submit recovery entered this path after the button disabled and navigation removed it: 23 reads, including repeated searches after the new screen had arrived.
TB Tree.write also requests activeRoot on every read even though it uses that result only when the windows list is empty. Deferring that call is a small independent candidate.

Native TB per-read median was comparable to Speedrun. The strongest measured difference was request count. The profiling evidence does not establish that all remaining RPC time is accessibility traversal: it includes agent serialization, transfer and envelope parsing.

proposed_changes.change: Stop motion recovery when fresh observations establish completed navigation after a loading/disabled state; retain recovery for clipping, spring overshoot and displacement inside a surviving list.
proposed_changes.validation: First reproduce the loading-then-navigation recovery read storm with a fake driver; keep existing delayed-click, lost-tap, layout-shift and spring tests passing. Add a device check before claiming a gain.

proposed_changes.change: Add targeted fresh target validation on the agent for eligible stable targets, with window/identity and occlusion checks and full-tree fallback for ambiguous or complex selectors. Keep timing and first-key guards.
proposed_changes.validation: Preserve duplicate-ID, changing-window, overlay, event-silent animation, clipped-target and stale-token behaviors. Benchmark ordinary native and Flutter and run native adversarial scenarios.

proposed_changes.change: Reuse any full snapshot already acquired during post-action validation, tagged with generation and context; invalidate on changes. Defer the unused activeRoot query when windows are present.
proposed_changes.validation: Verify recovery and snapshot history still receive owned complete snapshots, and that window/Compose freshness is unchanged.

proposed_changes.change: Consider compact binary or delta replies only after profiling agent tree acquisition and serialization separately.
proposed_changes.validation: Deltas require a resynchronization path for missed events, window changes and Compose updates; host decode alone measured very small here.

limitations: One sequential diagnostic run per condition, not a reliability or speedup benchmark. Native TB, native Speedrun, then TB Flutter. Each flow passed.

Counts are host-requested full hierarchy snapshots, excluding targeted focus reads, on-device settle probes and internal tree scans. Speedrun internal Restless tree probes may occur without a SCREEN request.

TB per-read timers include RPC and host driver decoding/construction, but exclude later runner history copying and matching. Post-reply host time excludes the wire envelope parse, which is inside the RPC timer.
Speedrun times are rounded to integer milliseconds by its debug logger. Its binary screen representation has fewer fields than TB.
Do not subtract cumulative read-time differences from flow time to predict a speedup: the tools perform different waiting and probing, and later waits can absorb time removed from earlier reads.
Production code and bin/tb were left unchanged; these are proposed optimizations based on measured evidence and pinned source review. Both emulators remain running.
